title: TSMC Commits to Ambitious Carbon Reduction Path in Line with Science Based Targets Initiative
gist: TSMC committed to SBTi-aligned absolute scope 1-3 cuts from a 2025 baseline, with emissions peaking in 2025, RE60 by 2030, RE100 by 2040 and net zero by 2050, backed by supplier programs covering ~90% of its supply-chain emissions.

insights.claim: TSMC's net-zero blueprint calls for peaking carbon emissions in 2025, returning to 2020 levels by 2030 with 60% renewable energy (RE60), reaching RE100 by 2040 and net-zero emissions by 2050.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Implies large, long-dated renewable power procurement by the world's largest foundry, relevant to Taiwan power markets and TSMC opex.
insights.quote: peaking carbon emissions in 2025, reducing them to 2020 levels by 2030

insights.claim: TSMC committed to the Science Based Targets initiative, setting absolute reduction targets for scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions from a 2025 baseline within the next decade, aligned with the SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Absolute (not intensity) targets constrain emissions even as capacity expands, raising the bar on clean energy sourcing.

insights.claim: TSMC's renewable energy usage surpassed 14% in 2024, leaving a large gap to its RE60 target for 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A ~4x scale-up of renewable share in six years signals heavy renewable PPA demand.

insights.claim: TSMC was the first semiconductor company to join RE100 and in 2023 pulled its RE100 target forward from 2050 to 2040.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Accelerated targets raise TSMC's exposure to renewable supply availability and pricing in Taiwan.

insights.claim: TSMC's overseas operations have achieved net-zero emissions for scopes 1 and 2 since 2022, and it consistently uses 100% renewable energy across global offices and overseas sites.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Shows overseas fabs can source clean power more easily than Taiwan, a factor in siting decisions.

insights.claim: TSMC reduces scope 1 emissions by upgrading local scrubbers and using carbon-neutral natural gas, and holds 53 LEED Gold-or-higher certifications, leading the semiconductor industry in certified building area.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Process-gas abatement is a recurring capex item for fabs.

insights.claim: TSMC pioneered a 20-year joint procurement agreement for 20,000 GWh of renewable energy to secure stable prices for suppliers and subsidiaries.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Long-tenor aggregated PPAs are a model that could expand renewable developer demand in Taiwan.
insights.quote: 20-year joint procurement agreement for 20,000 GWh of renewable energy

insights.claim: TSMC's 2024 supply-chain carbon reduction subsidy funds local Tier-1 raw material suppliers' equipment upgrades, targeting about 450,000 metric tons of emission reductions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: TSMC is subsidizing supplier capex, a modest cost that pushes decarbonization requirements down the chain.

insights.claim: Over 50 suppliers representing nearly 90% of TSMC's supply-chain carbon emissions have signed its GREEN Agreement, targeting RE85 for Taiwan production and RE100 for overseas production of products supplied to TSMC by 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Suppliers to TSMC face hard renewable sourcing mandates by 2030, raising their energy costs and green-power demand.
insights.quote: Over 50 suppliers have signed, representing nearly 90% of TSMC's supply chain carbon emissions

insights.claim: TSMC cites Industrial Technology Research Institute estimates that by 2030 every kWh TSMC uses producing HPC-related chips saves 6.8 kWh globally.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Supports an ESG narrative that advanced-node chips are net energy savers, useful against data-center power criticism.

top_entities: Greenhouse Gas Reduction, Emissions Elimination & Neutrality (GREEN) Agreement
